text:
Maya (Support): Jonah from Acme just escalated — their pricing assistant is returning much shorter, safety-averse replies since last night. Customer says it now refuses to suggest ranges and gives 'I cannot help with that' more often. They saw the behavior start ~2026-03-12 22:10 UTC. attaching steps and a sample convo from customer.

Jonah (Customer): @Maya yep. This literally broke our product experience. Before rollout it suggested tiered price ranges and follow-ups. After the update it says 'I can't provide that' or gives blank one-liners. Our customers are churning. Please escalate.

Maya (Support): I tried a quick repro using their prompt and our hosted API with their API key — got the same bland refusals. Posting the request body we used: 

```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses
{
  "model": "rwd-3b-chat",
  "input": "Suggest three price tiers for a B2B SaaS subscription and follow-up questions.",
  "temperature": 0.15,
  "top_p": 0.0,
  "max_tokens": 180
}
```

Maya (Support): Notably `top_p` is 0.0 and `temperature` 0.15 in the response metadata. That seems odd — customer didn't set top_p in their app, they rely on service defaults.

Dan (ML Eng): pinging. Did the defaults change in the config rollout last night? I wasn't on the canary.

deploy-bot: canary rollout completed: service=runtime-config, change_id=chg-20260312-11, applied "sampling_profile: safety_low" -> 03:22 UTC (+console link) :rocket:

Priya (SRE): I can see the same change in the config store: `sampling_profile: safety_low` replaced `sampling_profile: balanced`. The change was part of chg-20260312-11.

Dan (ML Eng): That `safety_low` profile forces `top_p=0.0` and `temperature=0.15` as defaults for hosted API when user doesn't override. It was meant to reduce hallucinations for certain internal evaluators, but it wasn't flagged as global default. My bad — I should've gated it.

Avery (EngMgr): Oof. How many customers were affected? Is this only hosted or also Dedicated/Private?

Priya (SRE): Only the hosted default key `service.defaults.sampling_profile` was swapped in the canary and then promoted. Dedicated/private customers that pin configs are unaffected. I can scope telemetry: queries where request body omits `temperature`/`top_p` but response metadata shows top_p==0.0.

Zach (Support Eng): Jonah, sorry about this. We're rolling back the sampling_profile to `balanced` immediately. ETA?

Dan (ML Eng): Rolling back now. Command I'm running: 

```
redwoodctl config set service.defaults.sampling_profile balanced --change-msg "rollback: revert safety_low default after customer regressions" --author dan
redwoodctl rollout promote chg-20260312-11 --undo
```

deploy-bot: rollback started: change=chg-20260312-11 (undo) by Dan; affected: hosted-api default key; target rollout window: immediate.

Priya (SRE): Observability note — we should not do immediate global promos without live traffic gating. Creating an incident ticket now and throttling promo permissions.

Dan (ML Eng): After rollback completes, I'm going to patch sampling profiles to require an explicit flag to become global default. Also adding automatic A/B checks: if %increase of refusals > 2x for top customers, auto-hold rollout.

Maya (Support): Jonah — we rolled back the default and will monitor your project; can you confirm if you see baseline behavior return? Apologies. Suggested reply draft to customer: 

"Hi Jonah — we identified that an internal sampling profile was mistakenly promoted as the global default during a canary. We've rolled that change back and are monitoring. I expect your assistant to return to previous behavior within minutes. We're also adding a guard to prevent this happening again. If you still see the issue please DM with an example convo and timestamp."

Jonah (Customer): Thanks. I'll re-test in 10m and post logs if still seen. Appreciate the fast response.

Ken (Product): Action items: 1) Dan to require explicit opt-in for any safety-oriented profiles before promotion. 2) Priya to add rollout gating check for customer-facing default keys. 3) Support to follow up with top 10 customers who might rely on defaults. 4) Add telemetry alert for "sharp drop in median response length" correlated with sampling_profile changes.

Avery (EngMgr): Also add a postmortem once stabilized. Let's include timeline, why the policy was missed, and how we changed dev/process.

Dan (ML Eng): Rollback completed: change chg-20260312-11 undone. I verified sample call now returns `top_p` unset in metadata and `temperature` back to 0.7 for default pipeline.

Priya (SRE): Monitoring metrics: median response length for affected orgs starting trending back up after rollback. Alerting window clear in ~12m.

Zach (Support Eng): Customer updated: Jonah reports restored behavior. He attached before/after examples; I'll archive them to the ticket.

Maya (Support): Closing loop — sending the drafted apology + postmortem crosslink once ready. Marking thread resolved unless we see reappearance. :white_check_mark: 

Avery (EngMgr): Nice work everyone. Please attach the canary logs and the changelist to the incident. We'll schedule a retro tomorrow.

Jonah (Customer): Confirmed fixed on our side. Thanks for the quick rollback and clear comms.
